clue.text: Elected to indicate if I am incapable? It's not important

parts.note: a candidate who has been elected is in office, so IN
to indicate something is to sign it, to give a signal
taken as written
someone incapable says 'I can't', written as ICANT

explanation.surface: A voter muses about admitting they cannot do something, then shrugs it off as trivial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'It's' are link words joining the charade to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trivial or negligible in size or worth is unimportant, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Write it in full

parts.note: in a pub order such as 'gin and it', the short word 'it' stands for a sweet red fortified wine from Italy; spelling that abbreviation out gives the full name

explanation.surface: An instruction to avoid abbreviations when writing something down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin and it' is a British cocktail order: gin with a sweet Italian fortified wine, the 'it' being short for its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The bar abbreviation 'it' expands to the name of the Italian fortified wine it stands for.

clue.text: Composer so associated with his country

parts.note: taken as written
the composer was American, so his country is the USA

explanation.surface: A composer is closely identified with his homeland.
explanation.definitionFit: John Philip Sousa was the American composer of marches such as The Stars and Stripes Forever.

clue.text: Former colony, now part of Queensland

definitions.meaning: the British West African colony that became Ghana in 1957
a coastal city and resort strip in the Australian state of Queensland

explanation.definitionFit: The same name belonged to the colony that became Ghana and now to an Australian resort city.

clue.text: Lay it on thick — I am finished and old

explanation.surface: Someone exaggerating wildly while admitting they are old and done for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay it on thick' suggests flattery or exaggeration; here it is the painter's method of applying paint heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter applying paint in thick ridges that show brush or knife strokes uses this technique.

clue.text: I make a killing as a whisky producer

parts.note: taken as written
literally, to kill: slay

explanation.surface: A whisky maker boasts of making a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make a killing' reads as making a big profit; literally it means to slay. 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish Hebridean island is famous for its peaty malt whisky distilleries.

clue.text: In favour of authentic church music

parts.note: being for the genuine is the same as being against the fake: a word for against followed by a word for fake

explanation.surface: Someone backs traditional, genuine church music.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay works by opposites: 'in favour of authentic' is restated as 'against fake', ANTI plus PHONY.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiphony is music sung alternately by two choirs or groups, a feature of church liturgy.

clue.text: Random chaps in a crowd?

parts.note: the idiom for any ordinary people at all uses three common men's first names

explanation.surface: A question about some arbitrary men in a throng.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names three typical men's first names to mean just anyone, ordinary people at random.

clue.text: From this country, a right to re turn Japanese earthenware

parts.note: the Times is a British paper, so this country is the UK

explanation.surface: Japanese pottery comes back from Britain.

explanation.definitionFit: Raku is a type of hand-shaped, low-fired Japanese pottery used in the tea ceremony.

clue.text: Lines to copy inside part of jacket

explanation.definitionFit: A lapel is the folded flap of a jacket's front below the collar.

clue.text: People engaged to protect new money resources

clue.text: Yes, an easy thing for city whiz kid

from 'easy as pie', a pie is something easy

explanation.surface: Making money is a doddle for a young City trader.
explanation.definitionFit: A young urban professional, the 1980s term for a high-earning young city worker.

clue.text: Criticise a match that's boisterous

clue.text: Professional ambition carries me all over the place

indicators.note: letters scattered in disorder are rearranged

explanation.surface: A person's drive at work takes them everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Careerism is putting one's career advancement above everything.

clue.text: In East, we become confused about a group of Pacific islanders

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the A
these words are muddled into a new order

explanation.definitionFit: The Taiwanese are the people of Taiwan, an island in the western Pacific.

clue.text: Classic ship-building material

oak trees supplied the timber for wooden warships

explanation.definitionFit: The Oaks is a Classic horse race, and oaks are the trees whose wood built sailing ships.

clue.text: One succeeds with song in audition

clue.text: Witnessing if youth leader is in-eluded in examination

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.walkthrough: 'in-eluded' is a scanning slip for 'included'; 'is included in' puts IF and Y inside TESTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Testifying is giving evidence as a witness in court.

clue.text: Like classical poetry chap is changing, adding extra page

these letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A man evolves, adding pages of verse in the classical style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' makes SAPHIC from CHAP IS; 'adding extra' slips P in.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapphic verse uses the stanza form of the Greek lyric poet Sappho.

clue.text: Devil's bound to be threatening

parts.note: an imp is a little devil; the 's links
a bound is a limit, an end

explanation.surface: The Devil is sure to be menacing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' reads as 'certain'; here it is a noun meaning limit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that impends hangs over us, about to happen, menacingly.

clue.text: Fruit becomes stale

definitions.meaning: the sweet fruit of a palm
something that goes out of fashion or fixes its era ages

clue.text: A person so cruel and so backward
